title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms
requirement: Landlords may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm, meaning one that uses nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old, to set rents or occupancy. No one may sell, license, or provide such algorithms to Berkeley landlords. Each unit-month is a separate violation, with civil penalties up to $1,000. Both the City Attorney and tenants may sue.
key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation (per unit per month)
coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential units in Berkeley and vendors of covered algorithms.
exemptions: Aggregated or anonymous reports that do not recommend rents. Affordable-housing rent or income limit tools. Market research for financing, appraisals, or software testing.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where the landlord uses a qualifying algorithm.

quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described
conflict_note: Sources disagree on timing. The ordinance PDF shows passage to print on 2025-11-18 and adoption on 2025-12-02, with no stated effective date. Morgan Lewis gives January 2026, consistent with the 30-day rule. The RealPage challenge was dismissed with prejudice on 2026-01-14.

title: Berkeley tenant screening fee rules (BMC ch. 13.78)
requirement: Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy or to add or replace roommates. Owners charging a screening fee must give, before receiving it, a clear Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and the state fee cap under Civ. Code § 1950.6(b). These rules apply notwithstanding contrary lease terms.
coverage_conditions: Owners and agents of residential rental property in Berkeley.
quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance – just cause
requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered units may be evicted only for an enumerated just cause. Measure BB adds the following limits. No eviction for nonpayment below one month's HUD Fair Market Rent. No eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar lease. Lease-breach evictions require actual harm and unreasonable conduct. Notices must reference Rent Board counseling and be filed with the Rent Board within 3 business days of service. A Notice of Tenant Rights is due within 15 days of the start of tenancies begun on or after 2024-12-20. Owner move-in evictions (and Ellis withdrawals, under the Ellis Implementation Ordinance) require relocation assistance, indexed annually: $19,413 standard plus $6,471 for qualifying households in 2026.
coverage_conditions: All fully and partially covered units, including new construction, single-family homes, condos, and subsidized units.
exemptions: Golden Duplexes. Units with a kitchen or bath shared with an owner who lived there at the start of the tenancy. Owner-occupied ADU properties (tenancies after 2018-11-07). Dorms. Nonprofit cooperatives.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemptions depend on owner occupancy (Golden Duplex, shared kitchen/bath, ADU), tenancy start date, and dorm/co-op status.

citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance (BMC ch. 13.76), as amended by Measure BB; Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance
quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”).
conflict_note: Measure BB's effective date is not stated. The 2026 relocation amounts are effective 2026-01-01.

title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance rent ceilings / Annual General Adjustment
requirement: Increases on fully covered units are limited to the Annual General Adjustment, set at 65% of the Bay Area CPI change and capped at 5% by Measure BB. The 2026 AGA is 1.0%, effective no earlier than 2026-01-01, for eligible landlords who meet Regulation 1148 conditions. Banked AGAs may be used. Capital improvement petitions are allowed only for completed work. For tenancies starting on or after 2024-02-06, utilities may be charged only within base rent or if separately metered in the tenant's name.
coverage_conditions: Units in multifamily properties with a certificate of occupancy on or before June 1980. Single-family homes whose tenancy began before 1996. Rooming houses with 5 or more rooms rented separately. Certain subsidized units.
exemptions: Partially covered (no rent ceiling): new construction with a certificate of occupancy after June 1980; most single-family homes and condos; Section 202/811 units; HUD-insured project-based units. Fully exempt: Golden Duplexes; units with a kitchen or bath shared with the owner; owner-occupied ADU properties (tenancies after 2018-11-07); dorms; nonprofit co-ops. The 2026 AGA excludes Costa-Hawkins tenancies begun on or after 2025-01-01.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Single-family homes and condos are covered only if the tenancy began before 1996. Coverage depends on subsidy type and HUD mortgage status. Golden Duplex, shared kitchen/bath, and ADU owner-occupancy exemptions apply. Landlord AGA eligibility depends on Regulation 1148.

citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76 (§ 13.76.110A), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024); Rent Board Reg. 1148
quoted_span: eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than
conflict_note: Sources describe the cutoff as both 'built before 1980' and 'certificate of occupancy after June 1980'; this record uses a certificate of occupancy on or before 1980-06-30. Measure BB's effective date is not stated. The 1.0% AGA applies to 2026 only.

title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
requirement: Housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or background checks in advertising, applications, selection, or tenancy decisions. Any action based on criminal history requires written notice and an opportunity to respond. Providers must post the Notice to Rental Applicants and Tenants. Penalties include fines of $1,000 to $10,000 per violation plus damages.
key_value: No criminal history inquiry or use
coverage_conditions: Rental housing providers in Berkeley.
exemptions: Owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units. Lifetime sex offender registrants. Limited exemptions for public housing and Section 8. Owner move-back agreements. Sublets and roommate additions.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Public housing/Section 8, owner move-back, and sublet/roommate exemptions apply.

quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
conflict_note: Passed 2020-04-14; the effective date is not stated.

title: Berkeley security deposit interest
requirement: For fully or partially covered units, landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits annually, plus a prorated amount at move-out.
coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
exemptions: Fully exempt units (Golden Duplexes, shared kitchen/bath with owner, owner-occupied ADU properties, dorms, nonprofit co-ops).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemptions depend on owner occupancy and dorm/co-op status.

citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance (security deposit interest)
quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.
conflict_note: The interest rate and code section are not stated.

title: Boston home rule petition for tenant eviction protections (H.3744, 193rd)
requirement: A home rule petition to authorize Boston eviction protections was sent to a study order and not enacted. It imposes no just-cause requirement.
coverage_conditions: Would have applied to Boston tenancies.
quoted_span: By Representative Montaño of Boston, a petition (accompanied by bill, House, No. 3744) of Samantha Montaño (with the approval of the mayor and city council) that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections.
conflict_note: Accompanied a study order on 2024-09-09; not enacted.

title: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act
requirement: Landlords and foreclosing owners ending a tenancy must give the Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources with any notice to quit or non-renewal. They must submit a copy of the notice and tenant contact information to the City via the online portal. The requirement cannot be waived. Penalties are a warning, then $300 per day; a violation does not halt the eviction.
coverage_conditions: All Boston landlords serving a notice to quit or non-renewal.
exemptions: Hospitals and health facilities; nonprofit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Triggered only when a termination notice is served.

citation: Boston City Code § 10-11.7 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
quoted_span:
The Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA) is an Ordinance passed by the City of
Boston in October 2020 that requires any landlord planning to end a tenancy
agreement to provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources.
conflict_note: Passed October 2020. Section 10-11.7 may be the penalty provision.

title: Boston home rule petition for rent stabilization (H.3744, 193rd)
requirement: A home rule petition to authorize Boston rent stabilization was sent to a study order and not enacted. It imposes no rent cap; G.L. c. 40P bars local rent control.
coverage_conditions: Would have applied to Boston rental housing.
quoted_span: By Representative Montaño of Boston, a petition (accompanied by bill, House, No. 3744) of Samantha Montaño (with the approval of the mayor and city council) that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections.
conflict_note: Accompanied a study order (H5035) on 2024-09-09; the session ended without enactment.

title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND-funded / IDP units)
requirement: Covered providers may not use blanket criminal bans. They may not consider non-conviction arrests, sealed or juvenile records, or convictions older than 5 years. They may not use credit scores; credit history may be used only in lieu of rental history.
key_value: No convictions older than 5 years; no credit scores
coverage_conditions: Providers with DND funding or land, BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy units, and the OFHE Affirmative Marketing Program.
exemptions: Convictions directly related to the housing or posing unreasonable risk. Federal or state requirements preempt.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: RESTRICTED: DND-funded or DND-land housing providers and BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units

citation: Boston DND Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
quoted_span: a) Arrests that did not result in conviction. This includes dismissed charges, diversion
conflict_note: This is an agency funding policy, not a codified ordinance.

title: Boston fair housing ban on rental assistance discrimination
requirement: Landlords may not refuse applicants or tenants because of rental assistance (e.g., Section 8 or veterans vouchers) or other protected classes. Enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission.
coverage_conditions: Housing transactions in Boston.
citation: Boston fair housing ordinance enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission (citation not stated)
quoted_span: The landlord tells you they don't accept rental assistance.
conflict_note: The page does not say whether the protection derives from the city ordinance or from G.L. c. 151B.

title: AB 325 Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms
requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade. A common pricing algorithm is one used by two or more persons that uses competitor data. No person may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or terms. This general antitrust law applies to landlords and rent software. Penalties are criminal and civil, including treble damages.
coverage_conditions: Any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm in California, including rental housing.
exemptions: End consumers. Single-firm algorithms that use only the firm's own data.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a common pricing algorithm is used as part of an agreement or with coercion.

citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
conflict_note: The effective date is inferred from the default January 1 rule; the bill was chaptered 2025-10-06.

title: California application screening fee cap and conditions
requirement: The screening fee is limited to actual out-of-pocket cost and may not exceed $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted from 1998 ($68.96 in 2026). No fee may be charged if no unit is available. A fee may be charged only under a first-qualified-applicant process or with a full refund to non-selected applicants (within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission). The landlord must give an itemized receipt and a copy of the credit report within 7 days. Unused portions must be refunded.
coverage_conditions: Landlords and agents screening applicants, guarantors, and cosigners for residential rental units in California.
exemptions: Does not preempt housing-assistance program fee rules.
quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
conflict_note: The current text was amended by AB 1170, effective 2026-01-01. The underlying cap predates this amendment, but no source states its original effective date. The $68.96 figure for 2026 comes from the Berkeley Rent Board.

title: Tenant Protection Act statewide just cause eviction
requirement: After 12 months of continuous lawful occupancy (24 months if adult tenants were added), an owner may terminate only for an enumerated at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the written notice. Curable violations require notice and an opportunity to cure. No-fault terminations require relocation assistance equal to one month's rent, paid within 15 calendar days, or a written waiver of the final month's rent. Owners must give a statutory notice of the rent cap and just cause protections in at least 12-point type. Noncompliance voids the termination notice.
key_value: Just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault
coverage_conditions: Residential real property statewide, including mobilehome park units, after 12 months of occupancy. Displaced where a qualifying local just cause ordinance applies.
exemptions: Certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years. Transient hotels. Care facilities and dormitories. Shared bath or kitchen with a resident owner. Owner-occupied single-family home renting no more than 2 units or bedrooms. Owner-occupied duplexes. Non-corporate separately alienable units with notice. Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires 12 months of occupancy. The separately alienable exemption depends on non-corporate ownership plus written notice. Owner-occupancy and shared-facility exemptions apply. Affordable housing is excluded. Displaced by qualifying local ordinances.

interaction: Yields to a stricter local rule in the same category where one covers the unit.
quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
conflict_note: The current section is operative 2024-04-01 and was amended by AB 1529 effective 2026-01-01. The original TPA just cause rules date from 2020, but that is not stated in the cited text. The section is repealed 2030-01-01.

title: Housing Crisis Act relocation for lower-income households displaced by demolition
requirement: Lower-income households displaced by demolition of protected units for new housing must receive relocation benefits equal to those public entities pay under Gov. Code § 7260 et seq. In Los Angeles, the higher of the HCA or city amounts applies.
coverage_conditions: Lower-income (80% AMI or below) households in protected units demolished for new construction.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: RESTRICTED: lower-income households in protected units demolished for new housing development

citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6(b)(4)(A) (SB 330, as amended by SB 8 and AB 1218)
quoted_span: the State’s Housing Crisis Act (HCA) require that ONLY lower income households being
conflict_note: The effective date is not stated in the source.

title: Tenant Protection Act (AB 1482) statewide rent increase cap
requirement: An owner may not raise gross rent over any 12-month period by more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower. The base is the lowest rent charged in the prior 12 months. No more than two increases are allowed per 12 months. Initial rent on a new tenancy is not capped where no prior tenant remains.
coverage_conditions: Residential real property statewide, including mobilehome park units for increases on or after 2021-02-18. Does not apply where stricter local rent control applies.
exemptions: Housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes). Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing. Dormitories. Owner-occupied duplexes where neither unit is an ADU/JADU. Separately alienable units (single-family homes, condos) not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, if the statutory exemption notice was given. Units under stricter local rent control.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The single-family/condo exemption requires a non-corporate owner and a written exemption notice. The owner-occupied duplex exemption requires owner occupancy. Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing and dormitories are excluded.

interaction: Yields to a stricter local rule in the same category where one covers the unit.
quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
conflict_note: AB 1482 took effect 2020-01-01 per the LAHD page. The current text (SB 567) is operative 2024-04-01. The cap applies to increases on or after 2019-03-15. The section is repealed 2030-01-01.

title: FEHA source-of-income protection and subsidy-applicant screening limits
requirement: Owners may not discriminate based on source of income, including Section 8, VASH, and other housing subsidies; 'No Section 8' policies are barred. For subsidized applicants, an income standard must be based only on the tenant's portion of rent. Credit history may not be used unless the applicant is offered the option of alternative evidence of ability to pay (SB 267). Income standards must count the aggregate income of co-residents.
coverage_conditions: Housing accommodations in California.
exemptions: An owner-occupant renting to one additional person. An inquiry about the level or source of income alone is not discrimination.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The credit history and income standard rules apply only to applicants with a government rent subsidy.

quoted_span: (a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
conflict_note: Subsidies were added to source of income effective 2020-01-01 (SB 329). The SB 267 credit-history provisions are effective 2024-01-01.

title: FEHA / Civil Rights Council limits on criminal history screening
requirement: No blanket bans on applicants with criminal records. Providers may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy safety, considering its nature and severity.
coverage_conditions: Housing providers and tenant screening companies in California.
exemptions: An owner-occupant renting to one additional person.
citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act; Civil Rights Council criminal history housing regulations (CCR section not given)
quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
conflict_note: The effective date comes from a secondary source (CAA). The regulation section number is not cited.

title: California security deposit cap and handling rules
requirement: The deposit is capped at one month's rent, furnished or unfurnished. Qualifying small landlords may charge two months, but not to service members; a higher service-member deposit must be explained and returned after 6 months. Deposits may not be labeled nonrefundable. The landlord must offer a pre-move-out initial inspection. Required photos: move-out photos from 2025-04-01, and move-in photos for tenancies beginning on or after 2025-07-01. Deductions are limited to unpaid rent, damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, cleaning to move-in condition, and restoration. Within 21 days the landlord must return the deposit with an itemized statement and receipts, plus proof of repairs from 2025. Return must be electronic if rent was paid electronically (from 2026-01-01). Bad-faith retention exposes the landlord to up to 2x the deposit plus actual damages.
key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords); 21-day return
coverage_conditions: Residential rental agreements statewide; the cap applies to security collected on or after 2024-07-01.
exemptions: Small landlord exception: a natural person or an LLC of natural persons owning no more than 2 rental properties with no more than 4 units total may collect 2 months, but not from service members.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The small-landlord two-month exception depends on ownership form and statewide portfolio size.

quoted_span: (c) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
conflict_note: The 2024-07-01 date is for the AB 12 one-month cap. The other subdivisions have staggered dates: proof of repairs 2025-01-01, move-out photos 2025-04-01, move-in photos 2025-07-01, electronic return 2026-01-01.

title: Cambridge Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance
requirement: Owners and managers must give the City's Tenants Rights and Resources Guide at the start of a tenancy and when taking steps to terminate it (notice to quit, summary process). The fine is $300 per day. This is a notice rule only, not a just-cause limit.
coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Cambridge, including tenancies at will.
exemptions: Hospitals and health facilities. Nonprofit short-term substance abuse facilities. Short-term rentals.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Excludes health facilities and short-term rentals.

quoted_span: The Ordinance requires owners, landlords, and management companies to provide you with information at the start of your lease or tenancy as well as when your tenancy is being terminated.
conflict_note: The page was first posted 2020-10-14; the effective date is not stated.

title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance (incl. source of income)
requirement: Landlords and agents may not discriminate in renting, viewing or tenancy terms based on protected categories, including source of income (Section 8, public benefits). Reasonable uniform standards such as ability to pay are allowed. Fines are up to $300 per violation.
coverage_conditions: Rental housing in Cambridge.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two-family dwellings.
quoted_span: Source of Income, includes Section 8 and public benefits
conflict_note: Summary page; no effective date given.

title: Hoboken ban on algorithmic rent coordination
requirement: Landlords may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms or occupancy.
coverage_conditions: Residential landlords in Hoboken.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where covered software is used.

quoted_span: Prohibits landlords from using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.
conflict_note: The secondary source cites 'ch. 158-2', and the effective month is from that source. The NJ FAIR Act may preempt this ban once effective (2027-07-01).

title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services (e.g., RealPage) that rely on nonpublic competitor data. Enforcement is public and private, with fines up to $2,000 per day.
coverage_conditions: Residential landlords in Jersey City.
exemptions: Reportedly excludes real estate agents.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where an algorithmic coordination service is used.

quoted_span: Prohibits a landlord s use of algorithmic rent coordination services; includes public and private enforcement; fines up to $2,000 per day.
conflict_note: The effective month comes from a secondary source. The NJ FAIR Act (effective 2027-07-01) bars conflicting municipal ordinances and may preempt this ban.

title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance (Chapter 260)
requirement: Rent increases on covered units are regulated under Chapter 260 (CPI-based) and administered by the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations. Increases beyond the standard limit require application (capital improvement, hardship). Tenants may file illegal-rent complaints.
coverage_conditions: Rental properties with 5 or more units.
exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties. Other exemptions by Rent Control Exemption Request. Under state law (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5), new multiple dwellings are exempt for 30 years after construction, and HUD/NJHMFA units are exempt.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Other Chapter 260 exemptions are granted by application. HUD-subsidized and NJHMFA-financed units are not subject to municipal rent control.

quoted_span: (Please Note: All 1-4 Unit Properties are exempt from rent control)
conflict_note: The allowable increase formula is not stated. The 30-year new-construction exemption comes from the DCA guide's statement of N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5.

title: Los Angeles RSO eviction grounds, notices and relocation
requirement: RSO units may be evicted only for enumerated at-fault or no-fault reasons. Nonpayment evictions require arrears above one month's Fair Market Rent (from 2023-03-27). Termination notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days. No-fault evictions require a prior Declaration of Intent to Evict and relocation assistance made available within 15 days. Relocation amounts for 7/1/2026–6/30/2027 are $11,000–$14,400 for eligible tenants and $23,150–$27,400 for qualified tenants, with reduced Mom & Pop amounts. A Notice of Right to Counsel is required from 2025-08-20. Demolition or conversion relocation is also owed under LAMC 47.06/47.07. Enhanced relocation applies to lower-income tenants of Protected Units demolished for new construction (Resident Protections Ordinance 188481/188482).
coverage_conditions: RSO units (first built on or before 1978-10-01, plus replacement units).
exemptions: Reduced Mom & Pop relocation for small owners doing owner/relative move-ins. No relocation for at-fault evictions.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Relocation amount depends on tenant age, disability, minor children, tenancy length and income. Replacement units are covered regardless of age.

quoted_span: Legal Reasons for Eviction
conflict_note: Relocation amounts reset each July 1. Bulletin A says the notice is filed within 3 days; Bulletin B says 3 business days.

title: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (non-RSO units)
requirement: For non-RSO units, after 6 months of tenancy or expiration of the original lease, a landlord may terminate only for enumerated at-fault or no-fault reasons. No-fault evictions require relocation assistance under LAMC 165.06. A JCO single-family home owned by a qualifying natural person pays one month's rent. A Declaration of Intent to Evict must be filed and notices filed with LAHD within 3 business days. The FMR nonpayment threshold applies. Landlords must provide the Notice of Renters' Protections (tenancies begun or renewed on or after 2023-01-27) and the Notice of Right to Counsel (from 2025-08-20).
coverage_conditions: Residential units in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO, including single-family homes and buildings newer than 1978-10-01.
exemptions: Transient hotels. Licensed care facilities. Fraternity/sorority houses. The owner's roommate. Certain co-ops, nonprofit and government-owned housing.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires 6 months of tenancy or lease expiration. Also covers older single-family dwellings alone on a parcel (not RSO). Owner's-roommate and facility exceptions apply.

citation: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance, LAMC § 165.00 et seq.
quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
conflict_note: The effective date and section numbers are not stated on the LAHD pages.

title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance allowable rent increase
requirement: RSO rent may be raised once every 12 months by the LAHD allowable percentage, which was 3% for 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30. From 2026-02-02, no additional utility percentage and no 10% increase for an added dependent are allowed. A 10% increase for an added non-dependent tenant remains, imposed within 60 days. RSO and SCEP fees may be passed through ($1.61 and $2.83 per month) after registration and notice. Larger increases require LAHD approval.
coverage_conditions: Rental units in the City of Los Angeles first built on or before 1978-10-01, plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28. Includes two or more single-family homes on one parcel, ADUs, and others.
exemptions: Rent is unregulated for condo/townhome tenancies begun after 1995-12-31. Luxury and temporary exemptions. A single-family dwelling alone on a parcel is not covered.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Replacement units are covered regardless of age. A lone single-family dwelling on a parcel is excluded. Condo/townhome tenancies after 1995 and luxury exemptions apply.

citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, LAMC Ch. XV, § 151.00 et seq.
quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage
conflict_note: The formula changed 2026-02-02, eliminating the utility and dependent add-ons. The 3% figure applied only through 2026-06-30; the LAHD calculator retrieved 2026-10-01 still shows it, and the 2026-27 percentage is not stated. The page keys coverage on 'first built'; the ordinance may key on certificate of occupancy.

title: Los Angeles RSO security deposit interest
requirement: Landlords of RSO units must pay interest on security deposits at a City-set annual rate (4.320% for 2025). Payment is monthly or annually, as direct payment or rent credit, and the method must be notified in writing.
coverage_conditions: Units subject to the Los Angeles RSO.
quoted_span: Interest Payments on Security Deposits
conflict_note: The 2026 rate is not shown. The effective date is the accrual start stated in the code text.

title: H.5222 – preventing algorithmic rent fixing (pending)
requirement: A pending bill would address algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing. It is not enacted.
coverage_conditions: Massachusetts rental housing (bill text not shown).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Bill text and scope unknown.

citation: Mass. H.5222, 194th General Court (new draft of H.1564)
quoted_span: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
conflict_note: Reported favorably 2026-03-12 and referred to House Ways and Means.

title: S.2983 – prohibiting algorithmic rent setting (pending)
requirement: A pending Senate bill would prohibit algorithmic rent setting. It is not enacted.
coverage_conditions: Massachusetts rental housing (bill text not shown).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Bill text and scope unknown.

citation: Mass. S.2983, 194th General Court (new draft of S.994 and S.1016)
quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
conflict_note: Reported favorably 2026-03-12 and referred to Senate Ways and Means.

title: Massachusetts ban on upfront charges beyond first, last, deposit and lock
requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a lessor or the lessor's agent may require only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month, and the cost of a lock and key. Application fees and other upfront charges are prohibited, and conflicting lease terms are void. Tenants have recovered treble damages for unlawful application fees.
coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies in Massachusetts.
exemptions: Vacation or recreational tenancies of 100 days or less.
citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B(1)(b), as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, §§ 54-55
quoted_span: (b) At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
conflict_note: The core limit dates from the 1970s. The 2025 amendment, effective 2025-08-01, extends it to the lessor's agents.

title: Massachusetts broker fee paid only by the hiring party
requirement: A licensed broker may contract with either the tenant or the landlord, not both. Any fee may be paid only by the party that engaged the broker. Under 254 CMR 7.00, brokers charging tenants must give written fee disclosure at the first meeting.
key_value: Broker fee paid only by the hiring party
coverage_conditions: Residential rentals in Massachusetts involving a licensed broker or salesperson.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a broker is involved.

citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 112, § 87DDD½, as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43
quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.
conflict_note: The 254 CMR 7.00 disclosure source is an archived secondary article.

title: Massachusetts notice-to-quit and nonpayment cure rules (no statewide just cause)
requirement: Massachusetts has no just-cause requirement. A tenancy at will ends on notice equal to the rental period or 30 days, whichever is longer, up to 3 months. For nonpayment, a 14-day notice to quit is required. Tenants at will may cure within 10 days, once per 12 months; written-lease tenants may cure by the answer date. A continuance of at least 7 days applies when nonpayment stems from government payment delays. Nonpayment notices must include the state form (§ 31), or courts will not accept filings.
coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in Massachusetts.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Cure rights depend on tenancy type and prior notices.

quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy; provided, that the tenancy of a tenant who has not received a similar notice from the landlord within the twelve months next preceding the receipt of such notice shall not be determined if the tenant, within ten days after the receipt thereof, pays or tenders to the landlord, the landlord's attorney, or the person to whom the tenant customarily pays rent, the full amount of any rent due.
conflict_note: These are procedural notice rules, not just-cause limits.

title: Massachusetts anti-retaliation (reprisal presumption)
requirement: Landlords may not retaliate for tenants' code complaints, enforcement of rights, or union activity. A termination notice (other than for nonpayment), rent increase, or substantial change within 6 months of protected activity creates a rebuttable presumption of reprisal. Damages are 1-3 months' rent or actual damages, plus fees.
coverage_conditions: Residential tenants in Massachusetts.
exemptions: The presumption does not apply to nonpayment notices.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires protected activity within the prior 6 months.

quoted_span: The receipt of any notice of termination of tenancy, except for nonpayment of rent, or, of increase in rent, or, of any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy within six months after the tenant has commenced, proceeded with, or obtained relief in such action, exercised such rights, made such report or complaint, or organized or joined such tenants' union or within six months after any other person has taken such action or actions on behalf of the tenant or in, or relating to, the building in which the tenant resides, shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities.

title: Initiative Petition 25-21 statewide rent cap (struck by SJC)
requirement: Would have repealed G.L. c. 40P and capped annual increases at the lesser of CPI or 5%. The SJC barred it from the November 2026 ballot (Cella v. Attorney General) because its religious exemption violated Article 48. It is not law, and c. 40P's ban on rent control remains.
key_value: Lesser of CPI or 5% (proposed, not law)
coverage_conditions: Most residential rental units statewide (as proposed).
exemptions: As proposed: owner-occupied buildings of 4 or fewer units; units less than 10 years old; certain publicly regulated units; short-term rentals; educational, religious or nonprofit facilities.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The measure never took effect.

citation: Initiative Petition 25-21; Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893 (2026)
quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%.
conflict_note: Struck 2026-06-23; one blog teaser says June 24. Proponents may refile, possibly in 2028.

title: Massachusetts housing discrimination ban including public assistance / housing subsidy
requirement: Landlords may not discriminate against recipients of public assistance or housing subsidies (including vouchers) or because of program requirements. They may not refuse to rent, or make inquiries, based on other protected classes. They may not refuse to rent to households with children.
coverage_conditions: Persons furnishing rental accommodations in Massachusetts.
exemptions: For § 4(7) and § 4(11): one unit in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling. For children: certain small dwellings with elderly or infirm occupants and temporary leasing of a principal residence.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The § 4(10) source-of-income ban has no owner-occupancy exemption; the other subsections do.

quoted_span: 10. For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient, or because of any requirement of such public assistance, rental assistance, or housing subsidy program.

title: Massachusetts security deposit law
requirement: The deposit may not exceed one month's rent. It requires a receipt and a statement of condition within 10 days. It must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, with a receipt within 30 days. Interest of 5% (or the bank rate) is paid annually. The deposit must be returned within 30 days of termination, less only permitted deductions with a sworn itemization, and transferred to a successor owner with notice within 45 days. An optional fee in lieu of deposit is allowed under EOHLC regulations, with fees plus deposit not exceeding one month's rent. Violations bring forfeiture and treble damages.
coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in Massachusetts.
exemptions: Vacation or recreational tenancies of 100 days or less.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Excludes vacation tenancies of 100 days or less.

quoted_span: (iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2);
conflict_note: Whether EOHLC fee-in-lieu regulations have been promulgated is not stated.

title: FAIR Act – Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent
requirement: Rental property owners and their agents may not pay for or use the services of a coordinator, meaning algorithmic revenue management software using competitors' nonpublic data to set or recommend rents, terms or occupancy. Coordinators may not facilitate anticompetitive agreements or parallel pricing coordination. Violations are violations of the NJ Antitrust Act, and an AG complaint portal will be created. Municipalities may not enact conflicting ordinances (§ 6(b)).
coverage_conditions: All owners of residential dwelling units used as a primary residence in New Jersey, and software coordinators.
exemptions: Government affordability controls. Research not used for pricing. Free public rent estimates. Equal-access brokerage databases. Non-AI spreadsheets. Medical, long-term care and correctional facilities.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where coordinator software is used.

conflict_note: Approved 2026-07-20; effective on the first day of the twelfth month following (2027-07-01). Section 6(b) bars conflicting municipal ordinances, which may preempt the Jersey City and Hoboken algorithmic bans once effective.

title: New Jersey rental application fee cap
requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge an application or similar fee above $50, CPI-adjusted annually from 2027-01-01. Penalties are $500, $750, and then $1,000, with refund to the applicant.
coverage_conditions: Residential rental property other than units in one- or two-family dwellings.
exemptions: One- and two-family dwellings. Real estate licensees unless the licensee is the landlord.
quoted_span:
1. a. A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.
conflict_note: The effective date is computed from approval on 2026-01-20 (first day of the fourth month following).

title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act good-cause requirement
requirement: A landlord may not evict or refuse to renew a lease without a statutory good cause, with a Notice to Quit (and a Notice to Cease where applicable). Illegal-occupancy evictions require relocation of 6x monthly rent. Self-help lockouts are illegal (N.J.S.A. 2A:39-1). Foreclosure is not grounds for eviction; new owners must give English/Spanish notice within 10 business days (2A:50-69). Eligible senior or disabled tenants in converted buildings may get up to 40 years of protected tenancy (2A:18-61.22). Landlords must distribute the Truth in Renting statement in buildings with 3 or more units (46:8-43).
coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals, including single-family homes, apartments, mobile homes, and rooming houses.
exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with 2-3 units and no more than 2 rental units. Transient or seasonal hotel guests. Units held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Transient/seasonal and disabled-family-trust exemptions apply.

quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.

title: New Jersey anti-reprisal protection
requirement: A landlord may not evict, substantially alter the lease, or refuse to renew in reprisal for a tenant enforcing legal rights, making good-faith code complaints, or joining a tenant organization.
coverage_conditions: Rental dwellings, including mobile homes.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
quoted_span:
A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of 
a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A. 
2A:42-10.10).

title: No unconscionable rent increases (Anti-Eviction Act)
requirement: There is no statewide numeric cap, but increases may not be unconscionable and must comply with any municipal rent ordinance. An increase takes effect only after a valid notice to quit and notice of increase.
coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units.
quoted_span:
The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
conflict_note: Municipal rent control may impose stricter caps. Under N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5, new multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control for 30 years.

title: No rent increases to cover condo/co-op conversion costs
requirement: In buildings converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, rents may not be raised to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion. Increases for new services or amenities are allowed.
coverage_conditions: All tenants in buildings undergoing conversion.
exemptions: Increases for new services or amenities.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to buildings undergoing conversion.

quoted_span:
If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee 
simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the 
conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).

title: New Jersey Fair Chance in Housing Act
requirement: Housing providers may not inquire about criminal records before a conditional offer. After an offer, they may consider only specified convictions within lookback periods (1st degree 6 years, 2nd/3rd degree 4 years, 4th degree 1 year; lifetime for listed crimes), with an individualized assessment. Arrests, expunged records and juvenile records may never be considered. No ads excluding people with records. No drug or alcohol testing of applicants. Penalties are up to $1,000, $5,000, or $10,000, enforced by the Division on Civil Rights.
key_value: No criminal inquiry before conditional offer
coverage_conditions: Housing providers of rental dwelling units in New Jersey.
exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of no more than 4 units. Methamphetamine production on federally assisted premises and lifetime sex-offender registration may be considered.
quoted_span:
shall not make any oral or written inquiry
regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
conflict_note: The effective date is computed from the 'seventh month' clause after approval on 2021-06-18.

title: NJ Law Against Discrimination – source of lawful income
requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or otherwise discriminate based on protected classes, including source of lawful income or rent payment (e.g., Section 8 vouchers). Fines are up to $10,000 for a first offense.
coverage_conditions: Rentals of real property in New Jersey.
exemptions: One unit in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling. Rooms in an owner-occupied single-family home. Certain religious and age-restricted exceptions.
quoted_span:
The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), 
N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires 
equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, 
ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, 
affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, 
nationality, or source of lawful income.

title: New Jersey Security Deposit Act
requirement: The deposit may not exceed 1.5 months' rent, including pet deposits and prepaid rent, and annual increases are limited to 10%. It must be held in trust in an interest-bearing NJ account, with written notice of the account within 30 days and interest paid annually. The landlord must return the deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions, within 30 days. The deadline is 5 business days after fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation. Wrongful withholding carries double damages.
coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals, including mobile homes.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in. Seasonal rentals of 125 days or less.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Seasonal rental exemption; tenant opt-in in owner-occupied 2-3 family dwellings.

quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

title: San Diego automated rent price-fixing prohibition
requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic devices that process nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy, and such devices may not be sold or licensed to landlords. Tenants may sue for damages, an injunction, and penalties up to $1,000 per violation. Each month and each property is a separate violation.
coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental property in San Diego; device vendors.
exemptions: Reports on aggregated nonpublic data more than 90 days old, or public data, that do not recommend rates. Affordable-housing program tools.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a covered algorithmic device is used.

quoted_span: San Diego similarly authorizes tenant suits for damages, injunctive relief and penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, with each month and affected rental property potentially constituting a separate violation.
conflict_note: The date and in-force status come from the Morgan Lewis summary (June 2025). The city's draft ordinance materials (O-2025-107, Feb. 2025) were used only for substance, not for dates.

title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections – just cause
requirement: From the start of a tenancy over 30 days, a landlord may terminate only for enumerated at-fault or no-fault just cause, with a cure notice for curable violations. No-fault terminations require relocation of 2 months' rent (3 months for tenants 62+ or disabled), paid within 15 days or waived. A 5-year right of first offer applies after certain no-fault evictions. Landlords must give a written tenant protections notice with the SDHC guide. Buyouts must exceed the relocation amount, with disclosures. Termination notices must be filed with SDHC within 3 business days, effective 30 days after the SDHC portal launches. Noncompliant notices are void.
coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in San Diego, including mobilehome-park units; tenancies over 30 days. Excludes fixed-term leases of 3 months or less.
exemptions: Certificate of occupancy within 15 years. Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (Section 8 still covered). Hotels and short-term rentals. Care facilities and dorms. Shared bath or kitchen with a resident landlord. Owner-occupied single-family homes renting no more than 2 units or bedrooms. Owner-occupied duplexes. Non-corporate separately alienable units with notice.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The separately alienable exemption requires a non-corporate owner plus notice. Owner-occupancy and shared-facility exemptions apply. Affordable housing is excluded. The SDHC filing requirement depends on the portal launch.

citation: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7 (§ 98.0701 et seq.; O-21647 N.S., amended O-21769 N.S.)
quoted_span:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
conflict_note: Amended by O-21769, effective 2024-03-28. The SDHC filing requirement (§ 98.0706(a)(2)) was not in effect as of 2023, and whether the portal has launched is unverified.

title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
requirement: Prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices that use nonpublic competitor data to set rents or manage occupancy. Tenants or the City Attorney may sue for damages, an injunction, and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation. Each unit-month may be a separate violation.
coverage_conditions: Residential units in San Francisco; sellers and users of covered devices.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a qualifying algorithmic device is used.

quoted_span: adding Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance went into effect on October 14, 2024. The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.

title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction and relocation
requirement: Landlords of covered units must have one of 17 enumerated just causes, and it must be the dominant motive. Lease expiration or a change of ownership is not just cause. Relocation applies to notices served 3/1/26–2/28/27. Under § 37.9C (owner/relative move-in, demolition, temporary capital improvement, substantial rehab): $8,245 per tenant, max $24,733 per unit, plus $5,497 per elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Ellis Act evictions under § 37.9A: $11,110.05 per tenant, max $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 per elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Temporary displacements under 20 days are governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9: $446 per day per household plus moving expenses.
coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance's eviction provisions, including post-1979 certificate of occupancy units and Costa-Hawkins tenancies that are exempt from rent limits.
exemptions: Units outside Rent Ordinance coverage (not enumerated in the source).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The unit must be covered by the Rent Ordinance eviction provisions; specific exemptions are not stated.

citation: S.F. Admin. Code §§ 37.9(a), 37.9A, 37.9C; Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9
quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.
conflict_note: Relocation rates adjust each March 1. The Ellis section number is inferred from a form label.

title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance annual allowable increase
requirement: For rent-controlled units, the annual increase is limited to the Rent Board's allowable amount. It is 1.6% of base rent for 2026-03-01 through 2027-02-28.
coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Ordinance's rent increase limits.
exemptions: Units first receiving a certificate of occupancy after 1979-06-13. Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies. Some units whose rent is regulated by another agency.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies (e.g., single-family homes and condos) and agency-regulated units are excluded.

quoted_span: 1.6% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
conflict_note: The rate resets each March 1 (prior rates: 1.4% for 2025-26, 1.7% for 2024-25). The certificate of occupancy cutoff comes from the SF just cause overview page.

title: San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance (affordable housing)
requirement: Affordable housing providers are restricted in how they may use arrest or conviction history of applicants and residents.
coverage_conditions: Affordable housing decisions in San Francisco.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: RESTRICTED: affordable housing providers/decisions

quoted_span: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.
conflict_note: The source is a one-line agency summary with no code section or effective date.

title: San Francisco security deposit interest
requirement: Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the Rent Board rate. The rate is 4.2% for 2026-03-01 through 2027-02-28.
coverage_conditions: Security deposits held for San Francisco rental units subject to the interest requirement.
citation: San Francisco security deposit interest requirement (S.F. Admin. Code ch. 49)
quoted_span: 4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
conflict_note: The Chapter 49 citation is not stated on the source page. Prior rates were 5.0% (2025-26) and 5.2% (2024-25).

title: Santa Ana ban on anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing (Ord. NS-3090)
requirement: Prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of algorithmic rent-setting devices that use nonpublic competitor data for residential rentals. Tenants may bring private claims for up to $1,000 per violation per month, plus attorney's fees. Code enforcement also applies.
key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation per month
coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential rental property in Santa Ana; device sellers and licensors.
exemptions: Software relying solely on public or aggregate historical data. Affordable-housing compliance tools.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a covered device is used.

quoted_span: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation and per month.
conflict_note: Sources differ. First reading was 2026-02-17 (PublicCEO, which reports it as pending). Final adoption was about 2026-03-03 (OCBJ, which says March 2026). Morgan Lewis gives an effective date of 2026-04-02, consistent with the 30-day rule.

title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
requirement: After 30 days of tenancy, an owner may terminate only for an enumerated at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in writing, with a cure notice for curable violations. No-fault terminations require 3 months' relocation assistance or a waiver of the final 3 months' rent. Owners must notify tenants of the protections at lease commencement or renewal.
coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in Santa Ana lasting more than 30 days.
exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years. Deed-restricted affordable housing. Transient occupancy. Care facilities. Dorms. Shared living quarters.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Deed-restricted affordable housing, transient, care, dorm and shared-quarters exclusions apply.

citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (2021)
quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.
conflict_note: 'Produced in the last 15 years' is not specified as construction date or certificate of occupancy.

title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance annual cap
requirement: Rent may be increased once a year by no more than the lower of 3% or 80% of the CPI change, and 0% if CPI is negative. The maximum is 2.87% for 9/1/2026–8/31/2027. Owners may petition for a fair-return increase. Owners must give written notice of the ordinance and tenant rights at lease start and with any rent increase notice.
coverage_conditions: Residential units in buildings constructed on or before 1995-02-01, and mobile home spaces offered for rent on or before 1990-01-01.
exemptions: Buildings constructed after 1995-02-01. Mobile home spaces first offered for rent after 1990-01-01.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Costa-Hawkins may exempt single-family homes and condos (not stated by the city).

quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period.
conflict_note: No municipal code section is given.
